generatedProse.concept-context: The School of Sport is a field of competing interpretations. A single finding, about a training effect, an injury risk, or a participation trend, can be read in more than one way, and scholarship advances when someone offers a reading others had not and defends it against the evidence. Creativity here is disciplined imagination: holding rival interpretations of a study in tension rather than adopting the most cited, and placing your own reading among them with reasons. A sport scientist, a coach and a management student may read the same figures and argue different conclusions, each from the evidence.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport management postgraduates discuss the same influential paper on a community participation campaign.

Tom summarises the paper's interpretation faithfully and treats it as established: this is what the literature says, so this is the position to adopt. The reading is accurate, but it is closed. No other interpretation is admitted, and Tom's own voice never enters; the discourse is reported, not opened.

Amara reads the same paper as one interpretation among several. One line of work ties the rise in participation to the campaign itself, another to a wider funding change, and Amara asks what each reading assumes and what it leaves out. Then Amara advances a reading of her own, argued from the evidence and placed explicitly against the others. The discourse has been opened up.

Both understood the paper. Only Amara treated interpretation as creative and contestable, and justified a voice of her own within the debate.
generatedProse.summary: Creativity in sport scholarship is disciplined imagination: reading a study as one contestable interpretation, opening up the discourse around it, and justifying a reading of your own against the evidence and the alternatives. You can now critique how creativity features in interpretation, appraise an interpretation by opening up its discourse, and defend your own voice in a debate. With the earlier lessons, you can treat creativity as a professional attribute, a mode of self-regulation, and a scholarly practice in the School of Sport.

check.body: You are writing about a key source in sport. Which approach best justifies your own reading as one creative voice in the debate?

items.text: Set the source against rival interpretations in sport and argue your reading from the evidence.
Adopt the source's interpretation because it is the most cited in sport.
Summarise the source as accurately as possible and add nothing further.
Assert your reading strongly without reference to other interpretations.

feedback.correct: That's right. In sport, you justify your reading by placing it against rivals and arguing from evidence.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the option that argues your reading against other interpretations.
feedback.incorrectFinal: A reading is justified by setting it against rivals in sport and arguing from evidence. Deference, bare summary and assertion do not.
